prerequisites: Programming (Programming Methodology, Programming Technologies and Paradigms)

learning_outcomes.text: Design and develop applications, ensuring their reliability, security and quality, in accordance with ethical principles and current legislation and regulations
Select and evaluate computer systems, ensuring their reliability, security and quality, in accordance with ethical principles and current legislation and regulations
Plan, conceive, deploy and direct IT projects, services and systems in all areas, leading their implementation and continuous improvement
Plan, conceive, deploy and direct IT projects, services and systems in all areas, assessing their economic and social impact
Prepare the technical specifications for an IT installation that complies with current standards and regulations
Knowledge, administration and maintenance of computer systems, services and applications
Knowledge of IT regulations at national, European and international levels
Apply redundancy in systems and installations
Measure and model system capacity and performance
Measure and model system reliability, availability, reparability, and security
Configure systems verifying multiple operating requirements
Assess the cost of capacity, redundancy and security when configuring systems
Document the technical-economic specifications of an installation in a statement of work
Specify and apply service level agreements

syllabus_topics: Introduction: System evaluation methodology, Selection of techniques and metrics
Performance measurement: Workloads, Monitors, Visualization, Instrumentation
Performance evaluation: Comparison of alternatives, Empirical models
Performance modeling: Analytical modeling and Simulation
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the practical part is 40% of the final grade (NPrac) and the final exam is 60% (NExa). To pass the practical block, a minimum score of 50% on NPrac and 80% attendance to practical sessions is required, and all four practical reports must be submitted on time. The final exam can only be taken if the practical part is passed, and a minimum of 50% on NExa is required to pass the subject. The final grade is calculated as Note = NExa * 0.6 + NPrac * 0.4. For extraordinary calls, students who have not passed the continuous assessment or have not attended it are evaluated, following the same criteria: 40% for the practical part (NPrac), which requires all four practice reports to be submitted at least one week before the exam date and a minimum of 50% on NPrac; and 60% for the final exam (NExa), which requires a minimum of 50% to pass. Fraudulent activity in any assessable test will result in a 0-Fail grade for the corresponding call.
